# Plot gallery and source links

::: {.doc-lead}
Find plots, insert them at their intended size, and keep their sources current.
:::

## Getting plots in {#getting-plots-in}

Plots reach a figure three ways: from the sidebar's **Plots rail**, which keeps the gallery
beside the canvas; from the full **Plot gallery**, a contact sheet for browsing a large
`plots/` tree; or by importing files and pasted images. Whichever way, every plot lands at its
[true physical size](/docs/semantic-plots.html#true-physical-size).

### The Plots rail {#the-plots-rail}

The sidebar's **Plots** view keeps your plots beside the canvas while you compose: the
**gallery** on top, and below it the [dissections](#dissections-pane) of whichever plot you
last clicked.

- **Alt+G** shows it and puts the cursor in its search box; it also opens a hidden sidebar.
  Press **Alt+G** again to go back to **Layers**. The two views keep their own widths (drag the
  sidebar's edge), and the canvas stays where it is when you switch. [Slides](/docs/slides.html)
  have the same rail beside the slide list.
- **Folders are headings**, not places you go into: every folder of `plots/` is a section you
  scroll through. Click a heading's arrow to fold it (deeper folders start folded);
  **Alt+click** a heading shows that folder alone. Type to search names and folders; **`_`**
  offers the companion collections (`_dissections`, `_lighttable`) — **Enter** goes in,
  **Backspace** in an empty search comes back out. **Proj** / **Glob** (**Alt+1** / **Alt+2**)
  switch between this project and your [global plot library](#global-plot-library).
- Plots sit at their true shape, several to a row, and every one is drawn on a background
  chosen so **all of it shows**: dark ink on paper, white ink (a plot made for a dark slide) on
  dark, both on grey, and a plot's own paper colour when it declares one. The **⋯** menu can set
  the background yourself (paper, dark, a checkerboard, or the figure's own), sort **Recent
  first** (newest-changed plots on top) and hide names. **Tiles → Gallery** and
  **Tiles → Dissections** size each pane separately (or **Ctrl+wheel** over it; **Reset sizes**
  goes back to 112 and 84 px).
- Typing anywhere in the rail goes to its search box, so tool keys never change your tool by
  accident. Files that appear or change in `plots/` show up on their own.
- While you work, Flux prepares the previews of the plots you have not scrolled to yet, a
  little at a time, so the next scroll or project open is instant. It pauses while you drag on
  the canvas, leaves very large files (over 2 MB) until you scroll to them, and stops for the
  session if a file crashes the preview renderer.
- Drag the line between the gallery and the dissections to share the height; drag it to an
  edge to fold a pane away; double-click it to reset.

### Read a tile {#read-a-tile}

Small marks on a tile tell you where a plot stands:

- **●** — the plot is placed in the active figure (dimmer: placed elsewhere in the project,
  with a count).
- **⧉ 12** — it has 12 dissection files; click the mark to show them.
- **◆** — an editable fluxplot (a [semantic plot](/docs/semantic-plots.html)).
- A **dashed outline** marks the plot selected on the canvas, and the rail scrolls to it
  (switch that off in **⋯**).
- An accent **dot** marks a plot that is new or was regenerated since the rail last listed
  it — handy after a re-run of your analysis. Clicking the plot clears it, and **⋯ → Clear the
  new-file dots** clears them all.
- **⋯ → Width class badge** adds the journal width each plot will print at: **1c** (one
  column, up to about 90 mm), **1.5c**, **2c** (full page, about 180 mm).

**Rest the pointer on a plot** for a moment to **peek** at it: a larger picture beside the
rail with its full name and folder, its printed size (in inches, as for matplotlib's `figsize`;
**Settings → Figure → Physical sizes** switches Peek and the Inspector to millimetres) and width
class, when it changed, where it is placed, its dissection folders, and why its tile has the
background it has. If the plot's ink would read poorly on the active figure's background, Peek
says so. **Shift+Space** peeks at the selected tile from the keyboard (and closes it again).
Peek never takes clicks and vanishes when the pointer leaves the rail; **⋯ → Peek on hover**
turns the hover off.

### Narrow the gallery {#narrow-the-gallery}

- **⋯ → Show only** filters to **Unused** (in no figure yet — slides are not counted),
  **Fluxplots** (editable ones) or **Has dissections**. Active filters show as chips under the
  search box; click one to remove it.
- Right-click a plot (or a folder heading) for **Show only this folder**; **Backspace** in an
  empty search climbs back out one folder at a time.
- **Similar names** lists a plot's variants across all folders (`_v2`, `_s07`, …), even from
  inside a folder shown alone; **Escape** returns to where you were.
- **⋯ → Stack variants** folds runs of variants in one folder — `fig1_a` … `fig1_f`,
  `latency`, `latency_v2` … — into one tile showing the newest, with a **×6** badge. **Enter**,
  a double-click or the badge opens the stack in place; the first variant's **◂** badge folds it
  again. Dragging a stack places the variant it shows.
- **Alt+/** switches the lower pane between Dissections and a **Folders** tree: the plot
  folders and how many plots each holds, with a search box for finding a nested directory.
  Choose a folder to show only its plots; **↑/↓**, **←/→** and **Enter** navigate and choose
  from the tree. The folder stays chosen while you flip to Layers and back. Companion
  directories stay out of this tree. **Alt+/** again returns to dissections.

### Place a plot {#place-a-plot}

**Double-click** a tile or press **Enter** to place the selected plots in the figure named at
the top of the rail (**→ Fig 3** — click it to pick another figure). **Drag** a plot onto any
figure to place it where you let go; over the canvas it shows at the size it will land.
**Space** opens a full-window preview. **Ctrl+Z** undoes a placement without leaving the rail.
When the rail is too small for the job, **Shift+Alt+G** (also from the rail's search box) opens
the [full gallery](#browse) in its own window.

### Dissections and notes beside the canvas {#dissections-pane}

The lower pane shows the [dissections](/docs/dissections.html) of the plot you last clicked, in
the gallery or on the canvas. Tables come first as small previews (a one-row statistics table
reads as a list), then each folder of panels; very large folders show a few and **Show all**.
If you were looking at a file (say `by_subject/s07`) and click another plot with the same
file, it stays selected in the same place, so you can compare subjects plot to plot. Clicking
an empty spot keeps the last plot showing; the **pin** keeps it while you click elsewhere.
**Double-click**, **Enter** or **Space** opens a file in the full
[Dissect viewer](/docs/plot-editing.html#dissecting-a-plot); drag a panel onto a figure to
place it. Plots from the global library show "Library plots have no dissections": dissections
belong to a project's `plots/_dissections/`.

**Notes** lets you create and edit ordinary `.txt` companions. Switch the pane from **Files**
to **Notes** and press **+ Note**; a plot can have several named notes. They save as you type,
and **Ctrl+S** saves now. The full Dissect viewer has the same **Notes** control. To search
their contents across the project, switch on **Notes** beside the gallery search and type a
word or tag such as `#check`; choose a match to select its plot and open the note here. If
another writer changed a note, Flux keeps your draft and explains the conflict before replacing
anything. See [Dissections](/docs/dissections.html#viewing-them) for the folder convention and
the viewer.

### Browse the full gallery {#browse}

The toolbar's **Gallery** button opens the full **Plot gallery** in place; **Shift+Alt+G**
opens it in its own window, from anywhere. It shows SVG and PNG previews in the current folder,
including GLB meshes marked **3D**. **Gallery** lays plots out as the Plots rail does — rows of
pages at each plot's own shape, under a folder header — and each subfolder previews the first
plots inside it, with a count. **List** shows one name per row. Adjust **Size**, **Space** and
**Names** to make the contact sheet comfortable; Size reaches **800 px** for large previews.
Flux remembers these display choices.

**Folders** shows or collapses a directory tree. Clicking a folder shows what is in it, and the
**›** arrow beside it expands or collapses its branches, so you can browse files without losing
your picks. **Clicking a gallery folder expands/collapses it**, in **Settings → Figure → Plot
gallery**, makes the click do both. The root button (**plots** or **plot_library**) returns to
the top, and **Up** or **Backspace** goes to the parent folder.

**◆** marks semantic plots and **◇** marks plain images; **List** also shows semantic and
paper-snip badges. In Slides, the gallery also previews MP4/MOV clips: select **Play video** to
play, pause, seek, or mute a clip in the full-window view (see
[3D and video in slides](/docs/slide-media.html)).

### Project and global plots {#global-plot-library}

**Project** / **Global** at the top of the gallery (**Proj** / **Glob** in the Plots rail;
**Alt+1** / **Alt+2** in both) switches between this project's `plots/` folder and your
**global plot library**, the `plot_library` folder inside your FluxConfig folder (by default
`~/FluxConfig/plot_library`). Picks from both scopes can go in together.

Put plots you reuse everywhere in the global library, such as logos, schematics, reference
panels and colour keys. Organise it with any folders you like, as you would a project's
`plots/`; Flux creates the folder the first time you open **Global**, and **Open folder** takes
you there. The project keeps its own copy of every plot you insert, and a global plot stays
linked to its file in the library, so regenerating it there updates it here on this machine.
The global library holds SVG, PNG and GLB plots; video clips live in a project's
`plots/_videos/`.

### Search, select and insert {#search-and-insert}

By default, search reaches ordinary folders throughout the tree you are browsing. **Search
reaches**, in **Settings → Figure → Plot gallery**, can widen or narrow that: everything in the
scope you are browsing (the default), only the current folder and its subfolders, only project
plots, only global plots, or everything in both. When results come from outside the scope you
are browsing, each one is labelled **Project** or **Global**.

The reserved [`_dissections/`](/docs/dissections.html) and `_lighttable/` companion collections
stay out of ordinary results. Type **`_`** to list them and **Enter** to go in, or open them in
**Folders**. Search then stays inside that collection until you leave it.

Click a plot, or press **Enter** or **Space** in an empty search box, to select it. Picks
survive folder changes and searches. **Ctrl+Enter**, the **Insert** button, or a double-click
inserts the selection.

**Ctrl+click** (**⌘+click** on macOS) a plot, or use **Preview** / **F4**, for a full-window
view. Arrow keys browse adjacent plots; **Escape** returns to the gallery. Open **Dissections**
or press **D** to inspect the plot's companion groups and panels. **Similar names** finds
filename variants across the current search scope, without selecting them; clear that filter to
return to normal browsing.

### Pin the gallery {#pin-the-gallery}

**Pin open** moves the gallery into its own resizable window (**Shift+Alt+G** opens it there
directly). Move it to another screen and keep arranging figures in the editor. The current
folder and selection are preserved, and you can still browse the entire `plots/` tree and the
global library. Insertions leave the window open and use the figure named in its footer;
successful insertions clear the submitted picks, ready for the next batch.

**Dock** returns the same gallery to the editor, and **Alt+G** brings an already pinned gallery
forward. **Refresh** reloads files and previews. Preview columns adjust as you resize the pinned
window, including while the editor is minimized. Closing the project also closes its gallery.

### Import from files or the clipboard {#import}

**Drag files in** from your file manager (an SVG with its `.fluxplot.json` sibling imports as a
semantic plot), use the toolbar's **Import** button (**Ctrl+Shift+K**), or **paste an image**
straight from the clipboard. A pasted image has no file behind it, so Flux keeps the original
for you in [`plots/pasted/`](/docs/project-layout.html).

Everything imports at **true physical size**: a 6.4 × 4.8 inch plot lands exactly that big,
never silently rescaled. If an import is larger than its figure frame, a notification says so;
**Ctrl+Shift+I** brings the selection inside the frame (moving it, never resizing it). To
change a plot's size afterwards, see [Resizing a plot](/docs/figure-layout.html#resizing-a-plot).

## Keeping linked sources current {#keeping-linked-sources-current}

Select a plot and press **Alt+Shift+C** to copy its full source path (with several plots
selected, one path per line); **Ctrl+K → Copy selected plot path** does the same. A plot
imported without a linked source copies the path of its saved SVG in the project.

Imported plots retain an accepted SVG and its semantic metadata in the project. When analysis
regenerates a linked source, Flux updates that accepted bundle automatically, including changes
only to a manifest or recipe. Figure, Paper, and Slides read the accepted version. Accepted
copies also catch up with their sources when the project opens and before export. Styling
overrides, figure identity, captions, and deliberate placement scale survive source updates.

The catalog's **Sources** section shows **Linked · current**, **Updating**, **Source missing**,
**Update failed**, or **Frozen version**. A missing or malformed source retains the last good
version; the error explains what needs attention. **Reload sources** retries immediately.
If a saved caption cannot be read, source refresh stops to preserve it. Restore access to
the caption file, then retry **Reload sources**.

**Relink…** chooses a moved source. **Freeze** gives the selected figure an independent saved
version; **Resume updates** links it again. These actions preserve the other figures' links.

**Used in** lists manuscript references and slide copies that share source assets. Removing a
referenced figure or canvas first shows these uses. Paper references then become unresolved;
slide copies retain the assets they need. A slide copy has its own layout and annotations.
